name: Kanye West
known_for: Roc-A-Fella soul-chop era (The Blueprint, The College Dropout, Late Registration), then 808s & Heartbreak and My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy; made the sped-up 'chipmunk soul' sample the sound of the 2000s.
techniques: Chops a soul or gospel record on an MPC grid and re-plays the chops in a new order instead of looping the record as-is.
Speeds the vocal sample up (pitch rises with it, often several semitones) so the voice becomes a bright, emotional hook: the 'chipmunk soul' sound.
Lets the MPC timing stay loose: off-beat kicks land slightly late for a lazy, human groove.
Big, hard drums under the soft sample: punchy kick, crisp snare layered with handclaps, sometimes a real drum break sampled under programmed hits.
Uses the human voice as the main instrument; later records add choirs, strings and horns for a cinematic build.
Filters the sample for the intro ('through the wall'), then opens it up when the drums drop; stutters a chop into the hook.
In the 808s era: Roland TR-808 drums, sparse minor chords, long booming 808s and vocal processing as texture.

params.harmony: Two-chord soul loop taken from the sample (often a minor chord and the chord a step below), bass doubling the sample's roots.
params.drums: Boom-bap: kick with late off-beat hits, snare plus clap on 2 and 4, swung 16th hats (about 54 to 58 percent), optional sampled break under it; hits_per_minute counts kick+snare events.

notes: No first-hand Kanye interview on technique was found in this pass; sources are track breakdowns (Reverb Machine), Soundfly and MusicTech overviews. The 'late off-beat kick' point is from the Good Morning breakdown. bpm, swing and hit counts are inferences. Medium-weak sourcing. Copyrighted records are never sampled here: P5 MIDI chops public-domain recordings (US, published before 1926) or royalty-free packs.
